question: Which disease is caused by excessive iron deposition within the reticuloendothelial cells of the liver, spleen and bone marrow?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hemosiderosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hemosiderosis** is a **medical condition **characterized by the accumulation of **excessive iron** in the **reticuloendothelial cells of the liver, spleen, and bone marrow**.
 
• This condition is marked by the deposition of iron deposits known as hemosiderin in various tissues. Hemosiderosis is commonly associated with secondary hemochromatosis and is frequently observed in individuals reliant on transfusions.
 
• While it often presents with no noticeable symptoms, some individuals may experience manifestations such as hemoptysis, iron deficiency anemia, diffuse pulmonary infiltrates, rapid breathing (tachypnea), difficulty breathing (dyspnea), paleness (pallor), rapid heart rate (tachycardia), bluish discoloration of the skin (cyanosis), crackling sounds in the lungs (crackles), wheezing, and fever.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Paresthesia** refers to an abnormal sensation experienced on the skin, characterized by tingling, pricking, chilling, burning, or numbness, without any discernible physical cause. Typically painless, paresthesias can manifest anywhere on the body, although they most frequently occur in the arms and legs.
 
• Ariboflavinosis is a condition resulting from a deficiency in riboflavin, also known as vitamin B2. While relatively uncommon in developed nations, it can affect up to 50% of individuals in developing regions.
 
• **Dermatitis** is a prevalent condition marked by inflammation and irritation of the skin. It presents in various forms and has numerous causes, often leading to symptoms such as itchiness, dryness, or the development of a rash.
